To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a variable-complexity multimedia streaming system that can be adapted for wireless multimedia applications.
we developed and implemented a video transcoding scheme for streaming videos to low-power mobile clients.
the Universal Tuner system can adaptively transcode MPEG-1 and MPEG-2 videos to BW or indexed color handheld devices, such as Palm OS, Pocket PC, and Win CE devices.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a variable-complexity video codec that can be adaptively partitioned to support the graceful degradation of video compression and decompression in mobile clients.
the design and implementation of a wireless video streaming and transcoding system for mobile devices.

the following issues: 1) the design of a low-complexity MPEG decoder for the Palm OS platform; 2) the design of an adaptive video streaming system to support variable complexity of the decoder; 3) the development of an adaptive video transcoding algorithm to support graceful degradation of the video quality in the presence of bandwidth and/or processing constraints.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our system is a novel and practical solution to the problem of video streaming over wireless networks to handheld devices with limited processing and memory capabilities.

the Universal Tuner project has successfully demonstrated the feasibility of implementing a wireless streaming video service on a low-power handheld device, and the feasibility of a variable-complexity multimedia codec design.
the proposed variable-complexity MPEG-1/4/2 video codec is a feasible approach to support the streaming of multimedia contents over the Internet to the mobile clients.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed the following:
A new variable-complexity video codec that can be used to adapt the complexity of multimedia codecs to the CPU processing capability of a client device.

we have designed, implemented and demonstrated the feasibility of a variable complexity video streaming system for the wireless handheld PDAs, and we have also developed a set of tools to facilitate the development of variable complexity multimedia applications.
the Universal Tuner project has developed a novel and practical approach to adapt the complexity of the MPEG-1/ 2 codec to mobile clients.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the complexity of the encoder can be reduced to a fraction of the original encoder without sacrificing much of the compression performance.
a variable-complexity video codec can be implemented on a mobile device by selectively disabling or reenabling stages of the algorithm.
we can achieve graceful degradation of multimedia processing algorithms on mobile clients with a variable-complexity multimedia codec.
